nodes.name: Dark console

nodes.name: Luminous dark

nodes.name: Quiet luxury

nodes.name: Neo-brutalist

nodes.name: Playful geometric

nodes.name: Warm organic

nodes.name: Glass layered

nodes.name: Poppy & Cream
nodes.notes: Poppy red-orange primary with a leaf-green accent on cream; playful retail, food delivery, brutalist menus.

nodes.name: Fraunces / Figtree
nodes.notes: Fraunces' soft old-style curves carry the personality at display sizes while Figtree stays quiet and even in running text; keep Fraunces upright and under 64px to avoid the oversized-italic-serif tell.

nodes.name: Instrument Serif / Instrument Sans
nodes.notes: Drawn as a family, the condensed high-contrast serif and the neutral grotesque share proportions, so headlines feel sharp without the body fighting them; use the roman, not the italic, for H1.

nodes.name: Newsreader / Source Sans 3
nodes.notes: Newsreader's optical-size axis keeps headlines crisp and decks readable, and Source Sans 3's humanist rhythm matches its transitional body shapes for long-form reading.

nodes.name: Source Serif 4 / Public Sans
nodes.notes: Two workhorse faces with matched x-heights: Source Serif 4 gives documents authority, Public Sans keeps UI and forms plain and legible, the kind of pairing legal and fintech products can trust.

nodes.name: Libre Caslon Text / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Caslon's sturdy old-style forms give headlines a printed-book weight and Work Sans, an early-grotesque revival, is period-adjacent without competing in texture.

nodes.name: Playfair Display / DM Sans
nodes.notes: A Didone headline needs a low-contrast geometric body, which DM Sans supplies; the classic magazine contrast works because the sans has no calligraphic stress to argue with (never swap in a humanist sans).

nodes.name: Cormorant Garamond / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Cormorant's small x-height and long extenders read as refinement at large sizes, and Hanken Grotesk's plain, slightly narrow grotesque recedes so the serif and the whitespace carry the page.

nodes.name: Literata / Albert Sans
nodes.notes: Literata was drawn for long screen reading and its optical sizes keep headlines from going spindly; Albert Sans adds a soft geometric counterpoint for UI labels without stealing attention.

nodes.name: Lora / Nunito Sans
nodes.notes: Lora's brushy, moderate-contrast serif and Nunito Sans' rounded humanist forms share a gentle calligraphic stress, so the pairing feels warm and organic rather than corporate.

nodes.name: EB Garamond / Onest
nodes.notes: Old-style Garamond and a humanist sans descend from the same broad-nib stress, so unlike Didone + humanist this is harmonious; Onest's slightly larger x-height keeps body copy modern.

nodes.name: Young Serif / Rethink Sans
nodes.notes: Young Serif's heavy, low-contrast letterforms behave like a display face so one weight is enough; Rethink Sans' clean geometry keeps the page from tipping into kitsch.

nodes.name: Gloock / Manrope
nodes.notes: Gloock is a single-weight Didone built for poster sizes, so pair it with Manrope's even geometric strokes at 1.414 scale and keep it to one or two lines per page; a humanist body would clash with its vertical stress.

nodes.name: DM Serif Display / DM Sans
nodes.notes: Designed as siblings, DM Serif Display's Scotch-roman contrast and DM Sans' low-contrast geometry share a skeleton, which is why the heading and body feel like one voice at two volumes.

nodes.name: Inter Tight / Inter
nodes.notes: Inter Tight gives the headline the tight tracking Inter lacks at display sizes so the family stops looking like an unchosen default; only use it with a distinct accent colour and real product imagery.

nodes.name: Geist / Geist
nodes.notes: One sans for everything with Geist Mono reserved for code, paths and IDs is the Vercel design.md recipe; the discipline is in the restraint, not the face.

nodes.name: Bricolage Grotesque / Figtree
nodes.notes: Bricolage's optical-size axis turns on its wonky display details only at headline sizes, and Figtree's smooth geometry below it keeps the quirk from infecting the reading text.

nodes.name: Schibsted Grotesk / Inter
nodes.notes: A newspaper grotesque with real character at headline sizes over Inter at text sizes gives a Swiss-grid page two distinct voices without leaving the grotesque family.

nodes.name: Plus Jakarta Sans / Plus Jakarta Sans
nodes.notes: A single geometric family at two weights is the quietest way to get a soft product voice; the slightly rounded terminals read friendly without needing pill-shaped type tricks.

nodes.name: Outfit / Nunito Sans
nodes.notes: Outfit's pure circles and verticals suit bright colour blocks and big rounded cards, and Nunito Sans softens the body copy so the page stays likeable rather than cold.

nodes.name: Sora / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Sora's wide, slightly squared geometry reads as technical on a dark canvas, and Work Sans' plainer grotesque keeps paragraphs neutral under glow and glass effects.

nodes.name: Host Grotesk / Funnel Sans
nodes.notes: Two 2024-25 Google releases nobody has defaulted to yet: Host Grotesk's compact grotesque headlines over Funnel Sans' open geometric text avoid the Inter-everywhere tell while staying strictly neutral.

nodes.name: Chivo / Be Vietnam Pro
nodes.notes: Chivo's heavy grotesque weights give headlines the punch a visible grid wants, and Be Vietnam Pro's cleaner neo-grotesque keeps body text from going muddy at small sizes.

nodes.name: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next / Atkinson Hyperlegible Next
nodes.notes: Built for low-vision readers with unambiguous glyphs, this family at two weights is the safe choice for dense tables and forms where character confusion costs money.

nodes.name: Archivo / Archivo
nodes.notes: Archivo's width axis lets the heading run condensed and heavy while the body stays normal width, so one grotesque does both jobs on a visible grid with hard edges.

nodes.name: Roboto Flex / Roboto Flex
nodes.notes: Roboto Flex's optical-size and grade axes keep 12px table text and 40px titles equally crisp, and its tabular figures line up in tight rows; one variable file covers the whole dashboard.

nodes.name: Manrope / IBM Plex Sans
nodes.notes: Manrope's rounded geometric headlines carry the product personality and IBM Plex Sans' slightly engineered grotesque keeps settings pages and forms businesslike underneath.

nodes.name: JetBrains Mono / Inter
nodes.notes: Mono headlines at a modest 1.2 scale read like a good terminal prompt rather than a gimmick, and Inter below them keeps prose and tables legible on near-black surfaces.

nodes.name: IBM Plex Mono / IBM Plex Sans
nodes.notes: Plex Mono and Plex Sans share widths and weights, so mono headings, sans prose and mono data columns align on the same baseline grid without visual seams.

nodes.name: Geist Mono / Geist
nodes.notes: Leading with Geist Mono for titles and captions and dropping to Geist for sentences gives bento cells and dark consoles a data-first voice while staying one coherent superfamily.

nodes.name: Space Mono / Space Grotesk
nodes.notes: Space Mono's quirky retro terminals make a deliberately unpolished headline, and Space Grotesk (its proportional sibling) carries the same DNA; reserve it for brutalist pages since Space Grotesk alone is now a default tell.

nodes.name: Martian Mono / Public Sans
nodes.notes: Martian Mono's width axis gives compact mono headers and labels that sit over dense tables, and Public Sans' neutral neo-grotesque handles the surrounding UI copy.

nodes.name: Azeret Mono / Albert Sans
nodes.notes: Azeret Mono is a chunky display mono built to be set large with thick borders and hard shadows, and Albert Sans' plain geometry keeps the body copy from adding more noise.

nodes.name: Syne / Manrope
nodes.notes: Syne's extended heavy weights are the image at poster scale, so everything else is small Manrope aligned to the grid; one headline per screen is the rule.

nodes.name: Unbounded / Onest
nodes.notes: Unbounded's ultra-wide geometric display letters fill a hero on their own; Onest's compact humanist body is the counterweight that keeps the rest of the page readable.

nodes.name: Archivo Black / Archivo
nodes.notes: Archivo Black is the fat grotesque neo-brutalism wants for flat fills and thick borders, and regular Archivo is literally the same design at text weight so the hierarchy is seamless.

nodes.name: Anton / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Anton's tall condensed caps pack a long headline into a tight block, and Work Sans' wider grotesque text opens the page back up beneath it; set Anton tight and never in italic.

nodes.name: Clash Display / Satoshi
nodes.notes: Clash Display's wide, slightly squared display forms give poster-type headlines a distinct 2020s brand voice, and Satoshi (same foundry) is a neutral geometric that stays out of the way; self-host both via Fontshare.

nodes.name: Cal Sans / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Cal Sans is the single-weight display face Cal.com ships for headlines; over Hanken Grotesk's plain text it gives a product page a clear, non-default headline voice at low cost.

nodes.name: Roboto Slab / Roboto Flex
nodes.notes: Roboto Slab and Roboto Flex share a skeleton, so slab headings over a flexible neo-grotesque body give documentation and dense admin pages structure without any stylistic seam.

nodes.name: Zilla Slab / Lato
nodes.notes: Zilla Slab's soft slab serifs (Mozilla's brand face) and Lato's warm humanist sans both have a slight calligraphic warmth, so the pairing feels approachable rather than mechanical.

nodes.name: Bitter / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Bitter was drawn as a reading slab for screens, so its headings stay soft and even, and Hanken Grotesk's quiet grotesque body keeps long articles calm.

nodes.name: System UI / System UI
nodes.notes: Zero font requests and native rendering on every platform; the right call for app shells, glass companions and data tools where the OS face is the honest choice.

nodes.name: System Serif / System Sans
nodes.fallback_heading: ui-serif, 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif
nodes.notes: New York on Apple and Georgia elsewhere give an editorial headline with no webfont cost, over the platform sans; useful for content sites that must be fast on first paint.
